clue.text: Drama student may be fast to embrace translated Greats

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so the word for fast wraps round the other letters

parts.note: fast means fixed firmly in place, stuck

indicators.note: translated suggests the letters of Greats turned into a different form, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone studying drama might be firmly committed to producing a version of classical Greats.
explanation.walkthrough: Greats is the Oxford classics degree, which the surface leans on; 'translated' is the anagram signal and 'to embrace' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone smitten with the theatre and longing to act, as a drama student may well be, is described this way.

clue.text: Foreman puts a toy train in packaging material

indicators.note: to train something is to shape or form it, so these letters are formed anew

explanation.surface: A foreman fits a toy train into some protective packing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like the toy itself but signals that FOREMAN PUTS A TOY is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: These small expanded polystyrene pieces are loose fill used to cushion goods in boxes.

clue.text: A sheet hung up by Bonxie, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue, hung up means the word for sheet is raised so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a sheet can be a sail on a boat

explanation.surface: A sheet has been pegged up by a seabird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hung up' turns SAIL to LIAS beneath the A. Bonxie is this puzzle's setter, and a setter's pseudonym is an assumed name; a bonxie is also a great skua, a seabird.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen-name such as Bonxie is an assumed name, a false name used in place of a real one.

clue.text: Flower pushed up through hole in slag heap, say

indicators.note: the reversed flower goes through, inside, the word for hole

parts.note: an eye is a hole, as in a needle

indicators.note: in a down clue, pushed up means the flower's name reads upwards

parts.note: a rose is a flower

explanation.surface: A plant has forced its way up through a gap in a mining spoil heap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' tempts as a river, but here it is ROSE; 'pushed up' turns it to ESOR, which goes 'through' EYE.
explanation.definitionFit: A slag heap is an example of an ugly thing that spoils the view, hence the 'say'.

indicators.note: put over means the word for large is turned round

parts.note: large and fat both mean big in size
feta is a Greek cheese

explanation.surface: A cloth has been laid over a big cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put over' turns FAT to TAF, placed above FETA in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp, lustrous woven silk or synthetic cloth.

indicators.note: out here means wrong or not in place, so the letters of steel nut are rearranged

explanation.surface: Discard a steel nut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw' reads as toss, but it is the definition in the sense of disconcert; 'out' rearranges STEEL NUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw someone is to disconcert them, to knock them off balance mentally.

clue.text: Cheap spice the pursuit of bell-ringers

parts.note: knockdown prices are cheap ones
ginger is a spice

explanation.surface: A bargain seasoning is what campanologists go in for.
explanation.walkthrough: KNOCK DOWN GINGER is a British children's prank of ringing a doorbell and running away, so the 'bell-ringers' are pranksters, not church campanologists.
explanation.definitionFit: The prank consists of ringing doorbells and fleeing, a pastime for mischievous ringers of bells.

parts.note: the rand is the currency of South Africa, a money traded internationally
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A money order sent abroad is out of the ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Something random lacks a pattern or regular method, so it is haphazard.

clue.text: Crowd outside pub turned up to see sport

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the assembled letters read upwards
the word for crowd goes round the outside of the word for pub

parts.note: a set is a group or crowd of people
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A throng outside a pub appears in order to watch a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' builds SINNET, and 'turned up' reads that whole word upwards, as a down clue allows.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport played over a net.

clue.text: Whenever in extremity, nature fights back

indicators.note: fights back suggests going in reverse, so the lodged letters are read right to left
in signals the letters are lodged within the words extremity and nature

explanation.surface: In dire straits, nature always retaliates.
explanation.walkthrough: The run EMITYNA sits in 'extremity, nature', and 'fights back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean at whatever time, on any occasion one chooses.

definitions.meaning: the cheetah is the fastest land animal, so a quick creature
a cheat is said to pull a trick of this kind, a deception

explanation.surface: A big cat is being towed along by a swindler.
explanation.definitionFit: The fastest land animal is a speedy beast, and pulling a quick trick on someone means cheating them.

clue.text: Layabout takes foreign cops a pancake

indicators.note: takes means the word for layabout holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a drone is an idler or layabout

indicators.note: foreign implies something strange or altered, so the letters of cops are rearranged

explanation.surface: An idler gives some overseas police officers a pancake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' turns COPS into PSCO, which DRONE 'takes' in.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop scone is a small thick pancake made by dropping batter onto a griddle, a British teatime item.

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, done for show only, nominal
a sign or indication of something

explanation.surface: A careless crossword hint.
explanation.definitionFit: A token gesture is a nominal, perfunctory one, and a token is also a sign or indication.

clue.text: Low Countries centre's subject to dispute

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

indicators.note: centre signals the middle letter of the word Countries

explanation.surface: The heart of the Netherlands and Belgium is a matter of argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low Countries' reads as the Benelux region, but 'Low' is the cow's MOO and 'centre' takes the middle letter of 'Countries'.
explanation.definitionFit: A moot point is one open to debate, unresolved and arguable.

clue.text: Cuts prize given to rugby players

parts.note: a medal is a prize
the Lions are the British and Irish Lions rugby union touring team

explanation.surface: An award is presented to members of a rugby side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuts' looks like injuries or reductions, but it means pieces of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Medallions are small round cuts of meat such as beef or pork.

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a kick is a thrill, a high
ness means a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A royal performs a bicycle kick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overhead kick' reads as a football move, but 'Over' is a positional signal for the down clue and 'head' means headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Highness is the formal style for a prince, as in His Royal Highness.

definitions.meaning: an assigned task or duty entrusted to someone
a fee paid to an agent as a proportion of the sale

explanation.surface: A fee is levied as a proportion.
explanation.definitionFit: A commission is a task one is charged with, and also an agent's fee taken as a share of a sale.

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the church part is left off

parts.note: the chancel is the part of a church near the altar

explanation.surface: An incomplete section of a church is opening.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening is an opportunity, a favourable chance to do something.

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing sizes

indicators.note: a hernia is a rupture, so the letters of hiatus are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Gentle manipulation helps a minor hiatus hernia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiatus hernia' is a real condition, but 'hernia' signals that HIATUS becomes HIATSU.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiatsu is a Japanese therapy of finger pressure on the body.

clue.text: It's forbidden to cut exposed vein

parts.note: out can mean not allowed, ruled out
to crop is to cut short

explanation.surface: Slicing open a visible blood vessel is not permitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vein' suggests a blood vessel but is a seam of rock showing at the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A vein of rock that protrudes above the ground is the geological feature named here.

indicators.note: losing his head means the clergyman's title drops its first letter

parts.note: a canon is a clergyman attached to a cathedral

explanation.surface: An unnamed priest has been beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for anonymous, it describes something with no name attached.

parts.note: N stands for number, an indefinite quantity in algebra
ether is an anaesthetic, something that numbs, so in crossword terms a numb-er

explanation.surface: The lowest pair of figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'numbers' is read twice: once as plain number, once as numb-er, a thing that numbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Nether means lower or underneath, so the bottom part.

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale
PH stands for public house, a pub

explanation.surface: Porter and pub both begin with the letter p.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks for P, but 'First letter' is the definition: the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleph is the opening letter of the Hebrew alphabet.

indicators.note: crunch means crush, so the letters of credit are crushed into a new order

explanation.surface: A ban imposed after the global credit squeeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'credit crunch' reads as the financial crisis, but 'crunch' rearranges CREDIT to ERDICT.
explanation.definitionFit: An interdict is an official prohibition, a ban.

definitions.meaning: to make something hurriedly, as clothes on a sewing machine
the preliminary period or charge before an event, as a bowler's or jumper's

explanation.surface: Rapidly build a way in.
explanation.definitionFit: To run up a dress is to sew it fast, and a run-up is the approach before a jump or delivery.

parts.note: a con is a swindle
a banker in betting is a sure thing, a cert

explanation.surface: A deal to cheat a financier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' suggests a financier, but in British betting slang a banker is a certainty, a CERT.
explanation.definitionFit: To act in concert is to act in harmony, in agreement.

indicators.note: a mess is a disorder, so the letters of EU Green are jumbled

explanation.surface: Reject the European Union's environmental muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: To renegue is to go back on a promise, to disown it; a variant spelling of renege.

clue.text: Young plants first wrapped in lighter packaging material

indicators.note: the pieces are wrapped in, enclosed by, the word for lighter

parts.note: a taper is a thin candle used to light things
issue means offspring, one's young

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of plants

explanation.surface: Seedlings are first wrapped in lighter packing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young plants' reads as seedlings, but 'Young' is ISSUE and 'plants first' gives P.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue paper is thin soft paper used for wrapping delicate items.
